display.purpose: Hero name only, typed in on load, followed by the amber caret.

body.purpose: All prose, list copy, contact links, stack values.

label.purpose: Lowercase section tags, timestamps/locations, header wordmark, stack row keys. Wide letter-spacing is the sole cue distinguishing it from body text.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: Hard-edged, non-eased hero caret blink; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: link-transition
motion.purpose: Link hover/focus shift toward signal amber; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: dust-field-mid
motion.purpose: Mid parallax dust layer, half the rate of the fine layer.

motion.name: dust-field-coarse
motion.purpose: Slowest, largest parallax dust layer, a quarter the rate of the fine layer.

components.name: Prompt-Prefix List Item
components.description: The `>` glyph opening every contact link and every now/experience bullet, the page's one recurring visual motif.
components.css: .ds-prompt-list { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; font-family: 'Departure Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 17px; line-height: 33px; } .ds-prefix { color: #7B7B7B; margin-right: 0.7em; } .ds-link { color: #E6E2D6; text-decoration-line: underline; text-decoration-color: rgba(230,226,214,0.4); text-underline-offset: 5px; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; transition: color 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), text-decoration-color 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-link:hover, .ds-link:focus-visible { color: #FFB000; text-decoration-color: #FFB000; }

components.name: Hero Caret
components.description: Amber blinking block after the typed-in hero name; the amber's first reserved use.
components.css: .ds-hero { font-family: 'Departure Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 5.1vw, 4.6rem); line-height: 1.1; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: #E6E2D6; } .ds-caret { display: inline-block; width: 0.52em; height: 0.82em; margin-left: 0.24em; vertical-align: -0.06em; background-color: #FFB000; animation: ds-caret-blink 1.06s steps(1, end) infinite; } @keyframes ds-caret-blink { 0%, 62% { opacity: 1; } 62.01%, 100% { opacity: 0; } }

components.css: .ds-section { display: grid; gap: 1.5rem 2.5rem; font-family: 'Departure Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; } @media (min-width: 768px) { .ds-section { grid-template-columns: 8rem minmax(0,1fr); } } @media (min-width: 1024px) { .ds-section { grid-template-columns: 11rem minmax(0,1fr); } } .ds-section-label { font-size: 16px; line-height: 22px; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: #7B7B7B; } .ds-section-body { max-width: 68ch; font-size: 17px; line-height: 33px; color: #E6E2D6; }

narrative.overview:
The site is a title screen, not a résumé page: one bitmap line holds still over a black field while dust drifts behind it, and everything else the visitor learns arrives by scrolling down through darker, quieter layers of the same void. There is no card, no rule, no divider anywhere in the build — every section boundary is made by vertical space and a label-sized left-column tag (about, now, experience, open source, stack, education), never by a box. Rank and recency are told by value (how bright a color sits between void and ivory), not by containment.

The palette is a single achromatic ramp from black to warm-white bone, broken by exactly one hue: a signal amber reserved for state, not decoration. Depth is conveyed by three things working together — brightness step, letter-spacing, and drift rate — never by shadow. The one font is a bitmap monospace (Departure Mono) at three sizes; there is no serif, no display face, no second family anywhere in the shipped HTML.
keyCharacteristics: One bitmap monospace face at three sizes (label / body / display), no display serif.
An eight-step achromatic ramp (void → ash → dust → frost → haze → mist → ivory) plus one reserved amber.
No shadows, no borders, no cards; depth is value + letter-spacing + drift, not elevation.
A live canvas of three parallel dust fields drifting at different rates behind all content.
`>` as the only recurring visual device: it marks every link-list item and every now/experience bullet, echoing a terminal prompt.

rules.name: The Amber Reserve Rule
rules.body: Amber marks state, never rank: it lights the hero caret and the current-role marker because those two things are alive right now, and it lights link hover, focus-visible, and selection because those are the browser's own state signals. It never appears as a decorative accent, a section marker, or a way to highlight a headline.

rules.name: The No-Chrome Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, border, or background fill other than void appears anywhere in src/styles.css or index.html. Section, card, and list boundaries are made with spacing and text color alone.

rules.name: The One-Face Rule
rules.body: Every piece of type on the page, from the hero name to a footer link, renders in Departure Mono. A second family is never introduced for contrast; contrast comes from size, tracking, and the color ramp.

rules.name: The Value-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy and recency are told by how light a text color sits on the achromatic ramp (ivory → mist → haze → frost) plus letter-spacing, never by shadow, border, or background elevation.

rules.name: The Experience Depth-Ladder Rule
rules.body: In the Experience list, each role's title steps one shade darker than the role above it as it recedes into the past — current role in ivory, the two most recent past roles in mist, the two earliest in haze, one entry reaching frost — and each role's bullet copy sits one ramp-step below its own title color. Letter-spacing on the title also widens slightly with each step back (0 → 0.02em → 0.04em → 0.06em → 0.08em).

dos: Do keep every new color on the eight-step void→ivory ramp; if a new state needs a hue, it is amber or it doesn't ship.
Do signal recency and rank with ramp position and letter-spacing, per the Experience Depth-Ladder Rule, before reaching for any other device.
Do open new link-list or bullet items with the `>` prefix in frost, matching every existing list on the page.
Do keep the dust canvas at z-index: 0 under a z-index: 10 content wrapper, and respect prefers-reduced-motion for any new motion.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow, border, background card, or divider rule anywhere; the No-Chrome Rule has no exceptions in the shipped build.
Don't introduce a second type family or a display-weight variant; the One-Face Rule means every size difference is expressed through the existing label/body/display scale.
Don't spend amber on anything that isn't the caret, the current-role marker, or a browser interaction state (hover/focus/selection) — it is not available as a highlight or accent color.
Don't round a corner. No element in the build carries border-radius.
